name: folio

scripts.pages:build: VITE_BASE=/folio/ npm run build && node tools/stamp-sw.mjs dist
scripts.author: node --experimental-strip-types tools/authoring/cli.ts
scripts.coverage:all: mkdir -p .coverage && { npm run coverage:unit >.coverage/unit.log 2>&1 || { cat .coverage/unit.log; exit 1; }; } && { npm run e2e >.coverage/e2e.log 2>&1 || { cat .coverage/e2e.log; exit 1; }; } && node tools/coverage-report.mjs --per-file

comment:coverage-combined: Combined coverage measured 97.87-97.92% over six runs (2026-10-31): five on the dev box and one in CI. It then rose to 98.00-98.04% once the e2e collected uncaught errors properly and three vacuous assertions were replaced with real ones. Floor is 97.5: 0.35pp below the lowest figure ever observed (97.85) and about 1.7x the measured 0.21pp band. The margin is deliberate and larger than the 0.06pp the old floor used: CON-COV-002 forbids lowering a floor, so an over-tight one has to be walked back and an over-loose one merely ratchets again. Drift, measured rather than inferred: the COMBINED figure has been observed between 97.85% and 98.08% across twenty runs (ten here and two in CI when this was first written, plus eight more across review rounds 5-11, which moved the TOP of the band to 98.08 as those rounds added tests). Re-measured rather than left behind: a recorded band that the current run already sits outside is a measurement going stale, and this repo's whole argument for the floor rests on the band being real. The LOWER bound is what the floor is set from and it has not moved — a 0.21pp band, about 18 lines of 8807. Underneath it the BROWSER half swings far more, 3965-4089 covered lines over six runs, because a session that renders slightly differently or a check that retries moves a hundred lines; most of that is absorbed by the union, since the unit half already covers those lines. src/shader.ts itself varies by three lines (150-153). An earlier version of this note said the three-line shader figure WAS the drift, which inferred the whole from one file (CON-DATA-001) — and it is the number the headroom argument rests on. The thing that USED to drift — destroy() and the webglcontextlost handler, 13 lines, once in three runs — is deterministic now: the e2e fires WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext() rather than hoping a page detaches the canvas before closing. The recorded cause for that swing (headless Chrome refusing a WebGL context) was wrong; a probe granted one 9 times out of 9. Never raise this on a single run.
comment:coverage-logs: coverage:all keeps the unit and e2e output in .coverage/*.log and CATS IT ON FAILURE, so a failing run prints its own diagnosis and a passing one stays quiet. Two earlier attempts were both wrong, in opposite directions. Redirecting to a file alone was worse than /dev/null in CI: .coverage is gitignored and the runner workspace is discarded, so the output stopped being visible anywhere. Piping to tee restored visibility and SILENTLY BROKE THE GATE — npm runs scripts under sh, which has no pipefail, so the pipeline reports tee status and a red e2e exited 0. run.mjs writes browser.lcov before process.exit(1), so the coverage figure would have looked almost normal and the job would have gone green on a broken e2e (CON-VER-001). `cmd >log || { cat log; exit 1; }` keeps the status and the output both.
comment:coverage-floor: coverage:gate hardcodes the floor rather than relying on `npm run X -- --min N`. The passthrough is npm-version dependent: it applied in CI and silently did NOT apply locally, which would have left the gate unable to fail after an npm upgrade. Hardcode, like test:gate.
comment:coverage: test:gate floors are a RATCHET — raise them in the PR that earns the improvement, never lower them to make a build green (CON-COV-002). These are the UNIT-only floors; the combined floor lives in coverage:gate and is documented above. Baseline 38.91/74.52/39.41 set 2026-09-20 when import-all first forced the whole of src/ into the denominator (the previously reported 87.65% measured only five files). Phase 1 raised it to 86.05/71.67/75.42 — branches fell because newly-covered files brought their unexercised branches into the denominator, which is the honest direction. Ratcheted again 2026-10-31 to 95.5/89/80. The figures first recorded here (three runs measuring 95.99 lines and 80.39-80.41 branches) do not reproduce and were not re-measured after later commits moved them: fourteen runs on this box since give lines 96.04 every time and functions 89.62 every time, while BRANCHES vary 80.30-80.45 (the 80.30 observed by review, 80.43-80.45 here). So the floors sit 0.54pp, 0.62pp and 0.30pp under the measured minima. The branch wobble is NOT a flaky test: it is src/fx.ts alternating 72.50 and 74.36, and the lcov shows why - BRH (branches HIT) is a constant 29 while BRF (branches COUNTED) is sometimes 40 and sometimes 39. Nothing the suite executes changes; V8 occasionally emits one branch range fewer for that file. That distinction decides the response: a suite whose outcome varied by order or timing would be a defect to fix under CON-VER-008, whereas an unstable DENOMINATOR is a measurement artifact to record and leave margin for. The branch margin is the thin one at 0.30pp, so raise the branch floor only off a re-measured minimum, and prefer earning the room back by covering some of fx.ts's 11 unhit branches; the floors had been left at 85/75/71 with eleven points of slack, in the very change that rewrote this note to say floors are a ratchet. This field used to say "Destination is 95" and "remaining climb to 95 needs browser-side coverage (shader/engine/tilt)": both were left standing after the combined floor passed 95 and reached 97.5, so the record contradicted the gate it describes — the same stale-note failure task 14c was closed for.
comment:author: The AI authoring pipeline (npm run author) needs @anthropic-ai/sdk. Install it on demand — `npm i -D @anthropic-ai/sdk` — it is not part of the app build.
